sources.entry: SABnzbd | Binary newsreader for automated Usenet downloads

summary.one_liner: SABnzbd is an open-source binary Usenet newsreader written in Python that automates downloading, verifying, repairing, extracting and filing files from .nzb files.
summary.what_it_does: SABnzbd takes an .nzb file and handles the rest of the Usenet download process automatically: downloading, verification, repair, extraction and filing. The README says it offers an easy setup wizard and self-analysis tools to check the setup. It is described as free and cross-platform ("works practically everywhere"). Dependencies include Python 3.10+, the Python modules in requirements.txt, par2 and unrar. The README also mentions multi-language support via a tools/make_mo.py script. It can run in the background as a daemon with a config file path option. The README also describes its git branching workflow and a privacy policy stating it does not transfer information to networked systems unless the user requests it.
use_cases: unpack and repair downloaded Usenet archives
set up a Usenet newsreader on a home server
how_to_run: Install Python 3.10 or newer, par2, and unrar (non-free official version)
notable: Fully automated pipeline: download, verify, repair, extract and file away with no manual steps after adding an .nzb
Setup wizard and built-in self-analysis tools to check the configuration
Background daemon mode with a configurable ini file
Privacy policy stating no data is sent to networked systems unless the user asks for it
caveats: Requires separate installation of par2 and the official non-free unrar
README covers running from source only; packaged installers are not described in detail here
Optional modules are only referenced via requirements.txt
